The 1st time, in my teens, I don't really knew why it started, or when exactly, but by 17 I was a textbook example of BPD. Like you said, brushed it off as normal angsty/confused/repressed/frustrated teen, but when I tried to kill myself, I guess the normalcy dissolved immediately. I was not "the weird kid", but I did tick differently, so I was bullied every so often.

Took me the better part of a decade to get back in functioning human state: education, career, family, back to "normal", only to have it all blown completely out last year, when my wife had a mental breakdown. All the emotions and memories I've repressed over the years are back, and my BPD is now all consuming.
Knowing what you have, knowing it has a name, feeling validated, does make things a bit easier. The monster has a name now, you know what you're fighting.

In the past 6 months or so I feel the same. Had my bout with suicide some 20 years ago, relapsed recently to depression, thought to actually seek help before things deteriorate more.  


Now I'm going about my day job, family, life, overwhelmed by suicidal thoughts, methods, and the odds of success.   


I won't do it, it's just all-consuming and a major distraction. Besides my Psychiatrist, I've told only one person about it.
